results.question: How much is the monthly fee on the everyday account and how do I avoid paying it?
results.answer:
The Kaskazi Everyday Account has a monthly fee of KES 250. It pays for running the account, the debit card, app and web banking, and your statements in the app.

You can avoid it in either of two ways, and only one needs to apply:
- **Salary:** The KES 250 monthly fee is waived for any month in which your salary is paid into your Kaskazi Everyday Account. Pay sent by your employer counts, but money you move yourself from another account, money paid in as cash, and money sent from a mobile money wallet do not count as salary.
- **Average balance:** The KES 250 monthly fee is also waived for any month in which your average balance is KES 50,000 or more. Kaskazi Bank adds up the balance in your account at the end of each day of the month, then divides by the number of days in the month.

If you'd like, I can check your current accounts and recent statement to see whether either waiver is likely to apply this month.

results.question: If I break my fixed deposit early do I lose my money?
results.answer:
No, you don't lose your deposit. You never lose any of the money you deposited by breaking a Kaskazi Fixed Deposit early. What you give up is part of the interest: you lose half of the interest earned so far. Kaskazi Bank pays you the other half, after withholding tax, together with the full amount you deposited.

Please note that breaking a deposit early is not a fee; you keep only half of the interest earned up to the day you withdraw. Also, you can't take out part of a Kaskazi Fixed Deposit. If you only need some of the money, breaking the whole deposit is the only option.

If you'd like to break a deposit, you can ask in the app, through this assistant, or at any branch, and the money is paid into your Kaskazi account.

results.question: what does 'up to 50 days interest free' actually mean? do I get 50 days on everything I buy with the credit card?
results.answer:
"Up to 50 days" means the number of days depends on when in the statement cycle you buy. The interest-free period runs from the day you make a purchase to the payment due date of the statement that purchase appears on. A purchase made on the first day of a statement period waits the longest before it is due, so it gets the full 50 days. A purchase made on the last day of a statement period gets the fewest days.

So no, you don't get 50 days on everything. For example, with a statement period of 1 to 31 May and a due date of 20 June, a purchase on 1 May gets 50 days, one on 15 May gets 36 days, and one on 31 May gets 20 days.

The free period also has a condition: it applies only when you pay your full statement balance by the payment due date. It does not apply to cash advances.

The one-third rule is the reason the app may cap your Salary Advance below 50% of your net pay. It protects you from being left with too little to live on. After your Kaskazi Salary Advance and its fee are repaid from your salary, you must still take home at least one third of your basic pay.

It matters most when your employer already takes large deductions. Your net pay is low compared with your basic pay, so the 50% figure would leave you with too little. To work out the most you can take under the one-third rule: take your net pay, subtract one third of your basic pay, and divide what is left by 1.03 to allow for the fee.

results.question: how is the personal loan interest worked out, is it linked to the base rate?
results.answer:
Yes, the Kaskazi Personal Loan rate is linked to the Kaskazi Base Rate. The Kaskazi Personal Loan interest rate is 15.5% a year. It is made of two parts: the Kaskazi Base Rate, which is currently 11.5% a year and is set by Kaskazi Bank, and a margin of 4.0 percentage points, which stays the same for the whole life of your loan.

Interest is worked out each month on what you still owe. Each month, interest is the monthly rate (15.5% divided by 12) applied to the balance you owe at the start of that month. Your instalment pays that month's interest first, and the rest reduces the balance.

If the Base Rate changes, if the Kaskazi Base Rate goes up, your rate goes up by the same amount and your instalment rises. If the Kaskazi Base Rate goes down, your rate goes down by the same amount and your instalment falls. We write to you in the app before the change takes effect, telling you the new rate, your new instalment and the date it starts.

If you'd like to see the exact instalment and total cost for a loan amount and term, I can work that out for you.

results.question: how long do you keep my data after i close my acount
results.answer:
